questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: BENEVOLENT
questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT means well-meaning and kindly; synonym = Kind. Opposite = Malevolent (evil) or Cruel.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: DILIGENT
questions.explanation: DILIGENT means having or showing care and conscientiousness; synonym = Industrious. Opposite = Lazy.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: ELOQUENT
questions.explanation: ELOQUENT means fluent and persuasive in speaking; synonym = Articulate. Distractor: Blunt means the opposite (plain-spoken without eloquence).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: FRUGAL
questions.explanation: FRUGAL means sparing or economical with money or food; synonym = Thrifty. Distractors: Extravagant and Lavish are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: GLOOMY
questions.explanation: GLOOMY means dark, despondent, or melancholy; synonym = Depressing. The distractors (Cheerful, Radiant, Bright) are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: HUMBLE
questions.explanation: HUMBLE means having or showing a modest opinion of oneself; synonym = Modest. All other options are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: INCESSANT
questions.explanation: INCESSANT means continuing without pause or interruption; synonym = Ceaseless. Distractor trap: Intermittent looks similar in register but means stopping and starting at intervals — the opposite meaning.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: ABERRANT
questions.explanation: ABERRANT means departing from the normal type or standard; synonym = Abnormal. Root: Latin aberrare = to wander away.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: ACRIMONY
questions.explanation: ACRIMONY means bitterness or ill feeling, especially in speech or manner. Root: Latin acer = sharp. Frequently tested in SSC and bank exams.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: AUDACIOUS
questions.explanation: AUDACIOUS means showing readiness to take bold risks; synonym = Daring. Root: Latin audax = bold. Opposite = Timid.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: BELLIGERENT
questions.explanation: BELLIGERENT means hostile and aggressive; synonym = Aggressive. Root: Latin bellum = war. A belligerent nation is one engaged in war.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: CAJOLE
questions.explanation: CAJOLE means to persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing or flattery; synonym = Persuade. Unlike 'Force', cajole relies on charm rather than pressure.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: CANDID
questions.explanation: CANDID means truthful and straightforward; synonym = Frank. Root: Latin candidus = white (pure). Frequently confused with 'Candied' which means sweetened.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: DEBILITATE
questions.explanation: DEBILITATE means to make someone weak or infirm; synonym = Weaken. Root: Latin debilis = weak. Opposite = Fortify/Strengthen.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: EPHEMERAL
questions.explanation: EPHEMERAL means lasting for a very short time; synonym = Fleeting. Root: Greek epi (on) + hemera (day) = lasting only a day. Exam trap: Eternal is the antonym.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: ERRATIC
questions.explanation: ERRATIC means not even or regular in pattern; unpredictable; synonym = Inconsistent. Root: Latin errare = to wander. All other options are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: FASTIDIOUS
questions.explanation: FASTIDIOUS means very attentive to detail and accuracy; difficult to please; synonym = Meticulous. Exam trap: Fastidious looks like 'fast' but has nothing to do with speed.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: GARRULOUS
questions.explanation: GARRULOUS means excessively talkative; synonym = Loquacious. Both are B2-level synonyms for 'talkative'. Opposite = Taciturn/Reticent.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: IMPEDE
questions.explanation: IMPEDE means to delay or prevent by obstructing; synonym = Hinder. Root: Latin impedire = to shackle the feet. Distractors (Help, Facilitate, Assist) are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: LETHARGIC
questions.explanation: LETHARGIC means affected by lethargy, sluggish, and apathetic; synonym = Sluggish. Root: Greek lethe (forgetfulness) + argos (idle). All other options are antonyms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: OBSEQUIOUS
questions.explanation: OBSEQUIOUS means obedient or attentive to an excessive or servile degree; synonym = Subservient. This word describes someone who is 'creepily eager to please'. Frequently appears in SSC CGL.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: PERFIDIOUS
questions.explanation: PERFIDIOUS means deceitful and untrustworthy; synonym = Treacherous. Root: Latin perfidia = faithlessness. Remember: 'perfidy' = betrayal. Classic exam word in SSC and UPSC.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: PULCHRITUDE
questions.explanation: PULCHRITUDE means physical beauty, especially of a woman; synonym = Beauty. Root: Latin pulcher = beautiful. The word sounds ugly but means beautiful — a common exam trap.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: RECONDITE
questions.explanation: RECONDITE means not known by many people; dealing with obscure subject matter; synonym = Obscure. Root: Latin reconditus = hidden away. Often appears alongside words like 'abstruse' and 'esoteric'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word CLOSEST IN MEANING to: SYCOPHANT
questions.explanation: SYCOPHANT means a person who acts obsequiously towards someone important in order to gain advantage; synonym = Flatterer. Root: Greek sukophantes = informer. Modern usage: a 'yes-man'. High-frequency word in SSC CGL and IBPS PO.
questions.subject: English
